messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'delta-3' p99 latency spike detected — 3.1x SLO. Streaming stalls spiking; queue depth rising. auto-escalation -> paging oncall. link: https://observability.redwood/pools/delta-3/graphs

sam (oncall): Seeing it. p95 ~ 420ms -> p95 SLO 200ms, p99 ~ 1.9s. Is this widespread or single-customer?

maya (cs): I'm getting reports from two customers in EU region (acme-inc, beta-voice). Both showing streaming disconnects and partial responses. Customer impact = partial streaming stalls (clients reconnecting).

raj (runtime): Jumping in. Initial checks: autoscaler triggered scale-up requests ~ 00:01:12 but warmup handshakes delayed. Kernel selection logs show repeated warmup coldpath hits and KV cache misses. Likely warmup + handshake lag causing tail latency.

nina (sre): Queue depth alert: queue depth jumped from 12 -> 240 over 60s for pool delta-3. Backpressure threshold breached. streaming-router shows many in-wait state.

sam (oncall): Immediate mitigations: 1) open canary fallback to pool-delta-2 for new sessions, 2) increase delta-3 min pool capacity, 3) temporary request-throttling for non-SLAd customers. Who can run commands?

lee (platform): I can run scale commands. Suggest set min instances to +4 and bump burst slots. Will also enable fast-failover routing policy for chat endpoints.

raj (runtime): Before scaling, quick check: we should try prefix-KV prewarm for top-heavy models (gptx-3b-q4). If warmup takes 20-30s per instance, scaling alone will not fix p99 immediately. We need routing fallback + cache prefill.

ops-bot: Command executed by lee: `redwoodctl pools scale --pool delta-3 --min-instances 8` (request id: r-9a4f).

lee (platform): done — min set to 8. Autoscaler still provisioning; ETA ~ 70s based on provisioning logs. I also enabled routing policy 'fallback-delta2' for the last-minute rollout.

raj (runtime): Running KV prefill for hot prefixes now (top 5 request prefixes from 10m window). Script:
```
# prefill script
redwoodctl kv prewarm --pool delta-3 --model gptx-3b-q4 --prefixes-file /tmp/hot_prefixes.txt
```
Triggered.

nina (sre): Observability note: streaming router p99 stalls dropped from 1.9s -> 1.2s after routing switch, queue depth down to 160. Not fully healed but improving.

sam (oncall): Good. Maya, please draft a short CS ping to affected customers: what happened, mitigations in flight, ETA ~5-10m. Triage message should emphasize we are not seeing data loss, only latency/stalls.

maya (cs): Drafted and sent to ACME + Beta-Voice. Will attach the incident link.

raj (runtime): Additional root cause note: autoscaler handshake logs show spike in 'handshake-time' metric to 45s at 00:01:10 correlated with a noisy neighbor allocation (node provisioning timeouts). Raising a ticket to infra for provisioning tail. Ticket: INF-4721.

lee (platform): Noted. For immediate risk reduction I'm enabling a temporary model-variant fallback (gptx-3b-q4 -> gptx-3b-q4-lite) for non-critical routes to reduce warmup cost. Enabling now.

ops-bot: Command executed by lee: `redwoodctl routing set --route /v1/stream/chat --policy fallback-delta2,gptx-3b-q4-lite` (request id: r-9a5b).

nina (sre): Metrics update — p95 now 250ms, p99 820ms, queue depth 48. Streaming stalls still present at low rate but majority of sessions healthy. Looks like routing + prewarm working.

sam (oncall): Marking incident as 'mitigated' for live customer impact. We'll keep page open for postmortem. Who's owning RCA?

raj (runtime): I'll lead RCA for runtime + autoscaler handshake. Need kernel selection dump, provisioning timings, and model warmup timelines. Assigning tasks: nina to collect provisioning traces, lee to collect autoscaler logs and policies, maya to collate customer impact windows.

nina (sre): Collecting traces now. Snapshot saved: https://observability.redwood/traces/trace-8c9d

lee (platform): Autoscaler logs archived at s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1829991111/autoscaler.tar.gz

maya (cs): Customer impact windows: ACME (00:00:50-00:03:20), Beta-Voice (00:01:00-00:02:40). Sent follow-up note with timeline and next-steps.

sam (oncall): Quick follow-up tasks before handoff: 1) post short status in #general, 2) spawn postmortem doc template, 3) if anything flares, page SRE escalation. I'll rotate to next oncall in 30m.

ops-bot: Posted status to #general: "Mitigated: delta-3 p99 spike. Routing fallback + prewarm + scale applied. RCA in progress."

raj (runtime): One more thing — root cause hypothesis: simultaneous large burst of short streaming sessions + cold KV cache combined with a slow node-provision tail created a feedback loop where autoscaler kept requesting nodes but warmup/handshake latency made nodes not join in time, amplifying queue. We'll validate with traces.

nina (sre): Agreed. Adding postmortem severity: Sev2 (customer-impacting, mitigated, RCA required).

sam (oncall): Thanks team. Handoff to raj/nina/lee for RCA. I'll remain available for clarifying customer timeline if CS needs. Closing live mitigation thread; keep this thread pinned to incident doc. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident thread closed for active paging at 00:23:20. Postmortem ticket created: PM-6842.
